page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an arm64-based virtual machine instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across four drives, while it lacks any integrated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 80 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography but lacking AVX or AMX vector extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a top-10% PassMark memory score of 3247.82. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, with read-only speeds reaching 314.24 GB/sec and write speeds at 120.6 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Compute performance is characterized by strong single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores of 1995.0 and 17128.0, respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong top-25% results. Database operations perform strongly with a PassMark database score of 26262.23, while standard CPU operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations align with middle-tier averages.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c4a-standard-16-lssd is driven by its high-density ARM architecture and the inclusion of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, which reduces the need for external block storage attachments for IOPS-heavy workloads. However, a notable tradeoff is the complete absence of AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets, which limits its utility for specialized x86 vector operations and heavy matrix math. Given the strong database benchmark results and high-speed local storage, this instance is suited for database hosting, text and image processing pipelines, software compilation, and general-purpose containerized workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and local NVMe performance.
